corrections.why: The register says the structure has fallen in on itself and Forest Lookouts lists collapsed ruins, so the site is not fully gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register describes a lookout-type cabin possibly used for fire watch; Forest Lookouts lists an AWS post; Willhite doubts it stood here in 1942 and suggests it was moved. The story reports all three and does not choose one.

Register gives Crown Pacific Timber Company; firelookout.com gives Washington Division of Forestry/DNR; Willhite found private timberlands with a gate. The story gives the register's name and says the land is private timberland today.
Register gives 1,179 ft (359 m); firelookout.com and Willhite give 1,198 ft. The record keeps 359.4 m from the register.

notes_for_editor: Identity is unclear: register says lookout-type cabin, Forest Lookouts says AWS post, Willhite says probably moved here after the war. Owner is also unclear: register says Crown Pacific Timber Company, Willhite says private timberlands (Campbell Group or Pacific West Timber in 2020) and that AWS records give the AWS cabin to Crown Zellerbach after the war. Willhite warns not to confuse this with the Neah site on the Makah Reservation (an 80-foot Coast Guard AWS tower), which is a separate site and was not researched. The brief's status 'gone' is corrected to 'ruins'. The site's gate and signs are described as restricted; the story advises checking with the landowner and does not encourage going past the gate. Used 1 web search and 4 page reads.
